quizzes.title: Ancient Worlds
quizzes.description: Pharaohs, emperors and lost cities from the dawn of civilisation.

questions.q: Which river was central to the civilisation of ancient Egypt?
questions.note: The Nile's yearly floods left fertile silt that made farming possible in the desert.

questions.q: Julius Caesar was the first Roman emperor.
questions.note: Augustus (Octavian) was the first emperor, from 27 BC; Caesar was a dictator.

questions.q: The Great Wall was built mainly to defend which country's northern frontiers?
questions.note: Most of the wall standing today was built during the Ming dynasty.

questions.q: Which Macedonian king, once tutored by Aristotle, conquered the Persian Empire?
questions.note: Accept Alexander the Great or Alexander III of Macedon.

questions.q: Which civilisation built the mountain city of Machu Picchu?
questions.note: It was built in the 15th century, probably for the Inca emperor Pachacuti.

questions.q: Where were the ancient Olympic Games held?
questions.note: They were held in honour of Zeus, traditionally from 776 BC.

questions.q: The pyramids at Giza were built as tombs for Egyptian pharaohs.
questions.note: The Great Pyramid was built for the pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BC.

questions.q: In which city is the Colosseum located?
questions.note: It opened in AD 80 and could hold around 50,000 spectators.

questions.q: Which Egyptian boy king's nearly intact tomb was discovered by Howard Carter in 1922?
questions.note: Accept Tutankhamen or King Tut.

questions.q: Cuneiform writing was developed by which ancient people of Mesopotamia?
questions.note: Cuneiform means wedge-shaped, from the marks pressed into wet clay tablets.

quizzes.title: Knights, Kings & Castles
quizzes.description: Battles, plagues and empires from the Middle Ages.

questions.q: In which year did the Battle of Hastings take place?
questions.note: William of Normandy defeated King Harold II and became King of England.

questions.q: Which famous charter did King John of England seal in 1215?
questions.note: It was sealed at Runnymede, beside the River Thames near Windsor.

questions.q: The Black Death swept through Europe in the 14th century.
questions.note: It peaked between 1347 and 1351 and killed perhaps a third of Europe's people.

questions.q: Which leader founded the Mongol Empire in 1206?
questions.note: Also spelled Chinggis Khan; his birth name was Temüjin.

questions.q: Which city was the capital of the Byzantine Empire?
questions.note: Today it is Istanbul; it fell to the Ottoman Turks in 1453.

questions.q: In which year was Charlemagne crowned Emperor by the Pope?
questions.note: Pope Leo III crowned him in Rome on Christmas Day.

questions.q: Joan of Arc fought on the English side in the Hundred Years' War.
questions.note: She fought for France and was burned at the stake in Rouen in 1431.

questions.q: Which traveller described his journey to the court of Kublai Khan in China?
questions.note: The Venetian merchant dictated his story while held prisoner in Genoa.

questions.q: Which Norse explorer reached North America around the year 1000?
questions.note: Accept Leif Ericson or Leif Eriksson; he was the son of Erik the Red.

questions.q: Which royal house came to power in England after the Wars of the Roses?
questions.note: Henry VII founded it after winning the Battle of Bosworth in 1485.

quizzes.title: The World at War
quizzes.description: Key moments from the two world wars of the 20th century.

questions.q: Which archduke's assassination in Sarajevo in 1914 triggered World War I?
questions.note: He was shot by Gavrilo Princip on 28 June 1914.

questions.q: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.
questions.note: It was signed on 28 June 1919, five years to the day after the Sarajevo killing.

questions.q: In which year did World War II begin in Europe?
questions.note: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939.

questions.q: Which US naval base in Hawaii was attacked by Japan on 7 December 1941?
questions.note: The attack brought the United States into the war.

questions.q: What was the code name for the Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944?
questions.note: Accept Operation Overlord; the D-Day landings began on 6 June 1944.

questions.q: Which British prime minister led the country through most of World War II?
questions.note: He took over from Chamberlain in May 1940.

questions.q: The Battle of Stalingrad ended in a German victory.
questions.note: The Soviets won in February 1943, a turning point on the Eastern Front.

questions.q: On which city was the first atomic bomb used in war dropped?
questions.note: It was dropped on 6 August 1945; Nagasaki followed on 9 August.

questions.q: What was the name of the German cipher machine whose codes were broken at Bletchley Park?
questions.note: Alan Turing played a key role in breaking its codes.

questions.q: Which 1916 battle saw nearly 60,000 British casualties on its first day?
questions.note: 1 July 1916 remains the bloodiest day in British Army history.

quizzes.title: Revolutions & Leaders
quizzes.description: Kings, liberators and statesmen who reshaped the modern world.

questions.q: Which French king was executed by guillotine in 1793?
questions.note: His queen, Marie Antoinette, was executed nine months later.

questions.q: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China in 1949.
questions.note: He made the proclamation in Beijing's Tiananmen Square on 1 October 1949.

questions.q: Who became the world's first female prime minister, in 1960?
questions.note: She led Ceylon, now Sri Lanka.

questions.q: The Battle of Waterloo, Napoleon's final defeat, was fought in which present-day country?
questions.note: Wellington and Blücher defeated Napoleon there on 18 June 1815.

questions.q: Which Egyptian president nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956?
questions.note: Accept Gamal Abdel Nasser; the move sparked the Suez Crisis.

questions.q: The Meiji Restoration of 1868 took place in which country?
questions.note: It restored imperial rule and launched rapid modernisation.

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi became independent India's first prime minister.
questions.note: Gandhi never held office; Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister.

questions.q: Who led Cuba after its 1959 revolution?
questions.note: Fidel Castro led Cuba for nearly fifty years before handing power to his brother Raúl.

questions.q: Which South American liberator is the country of Bolivia named after?
questions.note: Accept Bolívar or Bolivar; he was born in Caracas, Venezuela, in 1783.

questions.q: Who led the first Soviet government after the October Revolution of 1917?
questions.note: Kerensky led the Provisional Government that the Bolsheviks overthrew.
